newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares up as profit-taking wanes.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares up as profit-taking wanes.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial shares traded largely firmer on Tuesday with brokers saying the profit-taking which braked the market's month-long bull run last week seemed to be waning.

"I think the profit-taking is beginning to wane because a lot of institutional buyers are still underweight in equities," one broker said, echoing predictions by other brokers and market analysts that the wave of profit-taking would be short-lived.
"We are getting a second wave of buying and the market is starting to consolidate now and as long as interest rates continue weaker it will go ahead," he added.

The 57-counter industrial index surged 51.47 points to close at 6,766.45, pushed up mainly by sugar refinery ZS to 380 while tyre manufacturer Dunlop and tobacco company TSL put on 10 cents each to 210 and 510 respectively.

Against the trend, horticulture concern Ariston dropped 150 cents to 1,350, timber grower and processor Border and publishing group Zimpapers lost 50 cents each to 1,250 and 1,300 respectively while soft-drinks manufacturer Schweppes at 650 and tea producer Tanganda at 170 both shed 10 cents.
Minings were active but easier with gold producer Ashanti sliding 500 cents to 15,000. The seven-share mining index dropped 34.05 points to end at 1,325.21.
